title: In Hand Salary Calculator: Convert Your Hourly Rate to Annual, Fortnightly, and Tax Estimates
description: Use our in hand salary calculator to convert your hourly rate to annual pay based on a 38-hour week. Includes tax, super, and fortnightly estimates. Australian pay explained.
salarySummary: Based on a 38-hour week and 52 weeks per year, your annual gross pay is your hourly rate multiplied by 1,976 hours.

faqs.q: How is annual pay calculated from an hourly rate?
faqs.a: Annual gross = hourly rate × hours per week × 52. We assume a standard 38-hour week unless you adjust it. For example, $30/hour × 38 × 52 = $59,280 per year before tax and super.

faqs.q: What is casual loading and how does it affect my pay?
faqs.a: Casual loading is an extra 25% on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for lack of paid leave. If your base rate is $26.44 (National Minimum Wage), casual loading brings it to $33.05 per hour. Super is paid on the total including casual loading.

Super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid on top of your salary. For example, if your annual gross is $60,000, your employer adds $7,200 to your super fund, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830.

bodyMarkdown:
## Introduction

If you’re paid by the hour or considering a salary offer, the **in hand salary calculator** on this site helps you see the full picture: annual gross, fortnightly pay, tax, Medicare, and superannuation. Australian pay calculations can be confusing with different award rates, casual loading, and the super guarantee. This guide explains the key assumptions and figures so you can use the calculator with confidence.

## How the calculator works

The calculator uses a simple formula: **hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**. That gives your annual gross pay. From there, it estimates tax using the 2026–27 resident tax rates and the Medicare levy, then shows your annual, fortnightly, and weekly take-home amounts. Super is added on top at 12% of ordinary earnings, up to the maximum contribution base.

### The 38-hour week assumption

By default, the calculator assumes a **38-hour week** – the standard full-time week under the Fair Work Act. If you work different hours, you can adjust the weekly hours field. For part-time or casual workers, the same formula applies: just enter your actual average weekly hours. The calculator always multiplies by 52 weeks, assuming you work every week of the year with no unpaid leave.

### Fortnightly pay

Many employers pay fortnightly. The calculator shows your gross and net pay per fortnight (weekly × 2). For example, if your weekly gross is $1,000, your fortnightly gross is $2,000. This helps you budget and compare with salary offers that are quoted annually or monthly.

## Tax and Medicare

Tax is estimated using the 2026–27 resident tax rates:

- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income. The calculator uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed in this estimate. It does not deduct HELP repayments, the Medicare levy surcharge, or salary sacrifice arrangements.

## Superannuation

Super guarantee is **12% of your ordinary earnings**, paid on top of your salary. For example, if your annual gross is $60,000, your employer must contribute $7,200 to your super fund. The calculator applies this rate up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 (2026–27 figure). Super is not deducted from your take-home pay – it’s an extra contribution your employer makes.

## Minimum wage and award rates

The **National Minimum Wage** from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. This is set by the Fair Work Commission. Many employees are covered by **award rates** that are higher than the minimum. The calculator does not know your award – you need to check your classification on the Fair Work Ombudsman’s [pay guides](/blog) or your enterprise agreement.

If you enter a rate that matches an award or industry average, remember it’s an average, not a median for your specific job. For example, the Australian Bureau of Statistics’ Average Weekly Earnings for full-time adult ordinary time (May 2026) is $2,083.70 per week, but that’s an average across all industries and occupations.

## Casual loading

Casual employees are entitled to a **25% loading** on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for not receiving paid leave (annual, personal, etc.). On the [the timesheet](/) page, you can check a box to add 25% casual loading. **Do not enter a rate that already includes casual loading** – the calculator adds it for you. For the National Minimum Wage, the casual rate is $33.05 per hour ($26.44 × 1.25). Super is paid on the total casual rate.

## Using the in hand salary calculator

The **in hand salary calculator** is straightforward: type your base hourly rate (before any loading), choose whether you’re casual, and see your annual, fortnightly, and weekly estimates. The results include:

- Annual gross pay
- Annual tax and Medicare
- Annual super (employer contribution)
- Fortnightly gross and net pay
- Weekly gross and net pay

All figures are estimates. For a more detailed breakdown, see the [reference tables](/data) for tax brackets and super caps.

## Important notes

- The calculator assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice.
- Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base.
- Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds.
- HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted.
- This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax. Always consult a tax professional or the Australian Taxation Office for your personal situation.

## Conclusion

Whether you’re negotiating a salary, comparing job offers, or planning your budget, the **in hand salary calculator** gives you a clear starting point. Remember the assumptions: 38-hour week, 52 weeks per year, no penalties or allowances. Use it alongside the [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) and [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) guides to understand your full earnings picture.
